USER GUIDE
1. WHAT IS THIS MANIPULATIVE?
CIRCULAR COORDINATES & DYNAMIC PROJECTIONS
Trigonometry is not memorizing tables of static right triangles.On a unit circle of radius r = 1, circular coordinates are trig functions: (X, Y) = (cos θ, sin θ)Rotating the volvelle disc projects an angle θ directly ontohorizontal cosine and vertical sine windows with continuous precision!
CALIBRATED 84.00 MM RADIUS DATUM {xml_escape(dl)}\n{xml_escape(dl)}\n{xml_escape(dl)}\n{xml_escape(dl)}\n
DESK DISPLAY STAND LID & CADDY BAY
The 7U storage lid features an angled desktop easel stand with aprecision alignment cursor. Stand the volvelle on your desk whileworking through trigonometry, calculus, and physics assignments!
UNIT CIRCLE: 30° -> (cos = √3/2 ≈ 0.866, sin = 1/2)
ANGLE θ = 30° (π/6) X = cos(30°) = √3/2 ≈ 0.866 Y = sin(30°) = 1/2 = 0.500 Pythagorean Identity: cos²(θ) + sin²(θ) = 1 0.75 + 0.25 = 1.000

3. WHY KEEP THIS REFERENCE CARD?
✓ NO LOST PIECE LEFT BEHIND
Classroom manipulatives get lost. Never abandon an incomplete set! Every individual math component is permanently stocked for single replacements.
Scan back QR or visit stackcalc.io/parts Order individual replacement pieces anytime
✓ 10-SECOND SELF-CHECKING PACK-UP
Pack-up is a built-in math game! Align the transparent cursor to0° / 360°, slip the volvelle into its protective velvet caddy sleeve,and lay it flat into the box recess. Snap the stand lid shut.Lid latches firmly for silent, rattle-free carry.
✓ HANDS-ON TUTORIAL ON REVERSE
Flip this card over for a complete step-by-step hands-on lesson with concrete numbers, stage arrangements, calculator cross-references, and core mathematical principle breakthrough! Keep this card stored inside the box lid!
